 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ILESH J. VORA  Date : 07/06/2023  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This application is filed under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 by the applicant wife to transfer Family Suit No.124 of 2022 from the Family Court, Bhavnagar to the Family Court at Rajkot.
2. Heard Ms. Nimisha Parekh, learned counsel for and on behalf of the applicant.
Though served none has appeared for and on behalf of the respondent husband.

3. Facts and circumstances giving rise to filing of the present application are that the respondent husband has filed petition under section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act being registered as Family Suit No.124 of 2022 and the same is pending before the Family Court, Bhavnagar.

Prior to filing of the said Family Suit, the applicant wife has also filed a divorce suit before the Family Court, Rajkot and other proceedings claiming maintenance under section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

The Criminal Case registered under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is also Smitaben Miteshbhai Gohil D/O ... vs Miteshkumar Laljibhai Gohil on 7 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30059267/
1 C/MCA/1251/2022 ORDER DATED: 07/06/2023 pending before the Court at Rajkot.
4.

entities.text: Smitaben Miteshbhai Gohil D/O ... vs Miteshkumar Laljibhai Gohil
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In these background of facts, the applicant herein has preferred the present application.
She is having no substantial income and it is difficult for her to attend the Court proceedings at Bhavnagar.
The law with respect to transfer of proceedings, particularly matrimonial disputes, is no longer res-integra.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sumitha Sing vs. Kumar Sanjay, [2002 KHC 1889], Mona Aresh Goel v. Aresh Satya Goel, [2000 KHC 1835], Vaishali Shridhar Jagtap vs. Shridhar Vishwanath Jagtap, [ 2016 KHC 6489], Santhini V. Vijaya Venkatesh, [2017 (5) KHC 48] and Asiwarya N.C.V. v. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, [2022 (5) KHC 185 (SC)] held that it is the convenience of the woman and children that has to be looked into, while ordering the transfer of a case from one Court to another.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. In light of the law laid down in the aforementioned decisions, pleadings, the material on record and the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, particularly, the inability of the applicant to travel and appear before the Court at Bhavnagar and to meet the expenses of travel, I am inclined to allow this application.
Family Suit No.124 of 2022 is transferred from the Family Court at Bhavnagar to the Family Court at Rajkot.
Learned Family Court, Bhavnagar shall transmit the case record to the Family Court at Rajkot.
